NORTHWEST Orient AIRLINES

Hawaii
HAWAII —where the native language has no word for
weather*... where a tiny fish is called humuhumunu-
kunukuapua'a ... where more than three thousand spe-
cies of the exotic hibiscus flourish. where rainbows
have been known to appear in the full of the moon
Small wonder that "out of this world" is but a pallid
description of the spectacular beauty, the alluring
charm, the sheer fascination of these fabulous islands!
From the moment you first glimpse this patch of para-
dise from your airliner window until you reluctantly bid
the Islands aloha, you'll find your vocabulary hopelessly
inadequate to describe the beauty, the splendor, the
enchantment of Hawaii.
As you step from your Northwest Orient Airlines'
plane at Honolulu's oceanside International Airport,
and mingle with travelers from the four corners of the

The tem-
perature of the water at Waikiki Beach averages about 76
degrees in the winter; in summer, about 81.
Surfing at Waikiki is Year 'Round Sport
Hawaii is a land of sunshine and flowers
Hawaii has fine hotels to suit every taste
land of All-Year Sunshine!
world, you are greeted with Hawaii's traditional token
of welcome-a fragrant lei fashioned of orchids, gar-
denias, plumerias, jasmine or ginger blossoms. Of course,
as a visitor from the mainland, you neither need pass-
ports nor pay custom duties. Remember, this land of
lush superlatives is Hawaii, U.S.A., and you'll start
your thrill-packed vacation the moment you set foot
on Hawaiian soil.
To the uninitiated, the name Hawaii instantly brings
forth visions of Waikiki. Certainly, the Beach is worthy
of its fame, with its mile-long beach, its world-renowned
hotels, its daring surf riders-
-and its ukuleles! Yet, won-
drous though it is, Waikiki is but a small segment
of the incredible attractions which await the vacationer.
Several days can be spent in Honolulu itself (and all
Northwest Airventures provide a liberal amount of
free time for exploring this captivating city). Foremost
among the "must-see" sights in Honolulu are those
which represent a cross-section of the old and the
modern Hawaii. These include lolani Palace,
now
housing Hawaii's Legislature, the famous statue of
Kamehameha I, Queen Emma Home (Museum), the
Civic Center, the wide array of shops in the central
business district, the Kawaiahao Church, the Fish
Market, Punahou (Oahu College), the Honolulu
Academy of Arts, and, of course, Pearl Harbor.
But there's lots more to see on the island of Oahu, not
the least of which is the famous Nuuanu Pali, cer-
tainly the most spectacular beauty spot on the island,
and one of the geological wonders of the world. The
list of Oahu sights-to-see is almost endless, yet each of
the eight Hawaiian Islands offers its own version of
Nature's extravaganza.
On the island of Hawaii, the active volcano Kilauea
presents a sight which, for fierce beauty, is unsurpassed
On Maui, you'll see the "Home of the Sun,
" gigantic
Haleakala crater, big enough to swallow all of Man-
hattan Island! On the "Garden Island" of Kauai, you'll
be amused at Nature's practical joke... beaches of
"barking sands"! Yes, each of the islands has its own
story to tell, its own wonders to see-and wherever you
live in the U.S., you can be in this phenomenal land
of Ah's and Oh's in less than a day's travel —when you
fly Northwest Orient Airlines!
